memory_update.text: Energy Layer 1 should prioritize power availability, power delivery, and equipment bottlenecks across data centers, grid buildout, electrification, renewables, industrial load growth, and nuclear fuel-cycle constraints.

Highest-priority underfollowed nodes after Layer 1C are dry-type transformers, medium-voltage switchgear, power-quality equipment, HVDC reactors, transmission-line hardware, and grid voltage-control systems.

Second-order component nodes such as magnetics, power conversion, circuit protection, CTC magnet wire, bushings, tap changers, cores, and insulation remain promising but require more granular revenue and customer validation.

Reference leaders should be used mainly as evidence and pricing benchmarks; the main alpha discovery lane remains underfollowed suppliers and niche public companies one or two steps away from obvious AI/power demand.
Current Layer 1 universe is strongest in electrical/grid hardware and weaker in nuclear fuel-cycle, LNG/compression, gas turbine services, methane monitoring, and pipeline power-system subnodes.
Before Layer 2 ranking, each candidate needs primary-source evidence, current market-cap and liquidity checks, valuation/crowding checks, and a ticker/listing validation pass for non-U.S. names.

summary: Layer 1C merged universe for the Energy theme, treating energy primarily as a power-availability, power-delivery, grid-equipment, electrification, and critical-energy-supply-chain chokepoint rather than a simple commodity basket. The deduped universe prioritizes underfollowed electrical equipment, transformer, switchgear, transmission hardware, power-quality, HVDC, grid-interconnection, and second-order component names, while retaining a smaller set of reference leaders for benchmarking. Candidate ranking is based on Serenity relevance before full primary-source validation; no buy/sell recommendation is implied.
